clauses.text:
1-101. Establishment o f Board. There is established, effective immediately,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this 
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier.

1-102. Report  The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days of its creation.
1— 103. Maintaining Conditions. As provided by Section T O  of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 30  
days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by 
agreement of the parties, shall be made by the carrier or by the employees, in 
the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

1-104. Expiration. The Emergency Board shall terminate upon submission of  
the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

own_original_text:
Executive Order 12405 of February 14, 1983
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute 
Between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brother­
hood of Locomotive Engineers
À dispute exists between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brother­
hood of Locomotive Engineers.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted Under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a 
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the Act, as 
amended (45 U.S.C. § 160), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishment o f Board. There is established, effective immediately,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this 
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report  The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days of its creation.
1— 103. Maintaining Conditions. As provided by Section T O  of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 30  
days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by 
agreement of the parties, shall be made by the carrier or by the employees, in 
the conditions out of which the dispute arose.
1-104. Expiration. The Emergency Board shall terminate upon submission of  
the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.
THE WHITE HOUSE,

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12405 (48 FR 6889, Federal Register of February 16, 1983; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and signed February 14, 1983. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12405 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
